parsed_response.reasoning: The migration inserts each site setting value verbatim: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, with no scheme/path stripping. But `record_for_host` matches only via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against `uri.host`, and the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? specs (deleted in this diff) explicitly treated values like 'http://eviltrout.com' and 'https://example.com/1234' as valid settings. So migrated entries carrying a scheme or path can never match, silently denying embedding for previously-working hosts. The SQL interpolation also breaks on a value containing a single quote. Both mechanisms are verifiable directly in the diff.

judged_text: The INSERT interpolates each raw setting value without the scheme/path stripping the old allows_embeddable_host? applied and without the model's before_validation, so entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — both exercised as working values by the removed specs — are stored verbatim and can never match record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison. Upgraded sites whose working host entries carried a scheme or path end up with rows that authorize nothing (embedding silently denied for those hosts); a stored value containing a single quote additionally makes the INSERT raise a SQL syntax error that aborts the migration.
